speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to my talk.
zh: 欢迎来到我的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Joshua Moe, and today we're going to be talking about some of the challenges of building a privacy-respecting AI system.
zh: 我是 Joshua Moe,今天我们要讨论构建尊重隐私的 AI 系统所面临的一些挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just for an introduction as to who I am, I'm currently the Lead Developer Relations Engineer at Venice AI.
zh: 简单介绍一下我自己,我目前是 Venice AI 的首席开发者关系工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: So currently I handle partnerships, documentation, talking to developers, some engineering, and other things as well.
zh: 目前我负责合作伙伴关系、文档、与开发者沟通、一些工程工作,以及其他事务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So prior to this, I was actually the lead maintainer for RIG, which is the leading AI framework in Rust.
zh: 在此之前,我实际上是 RIG 的首席维护者,RIG 是 Rust 语言中领先的 AI 框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what is Venice?
zh: 那么 Venice 是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So Venice is a private and unrestricted AI platform.
zh: Venice 是一个私密且无限制的 AI 平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we host all the latest open source models.
zh: 我们托管所有最新的开源模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're 100% open AI compatible.
zh: 我们 100% 兼容 OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't store any prompts or conversations.
zh: 我们不存储任何提示词或对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also have a web app that you can use to talk to our models as well.
zh: 我们还有一个网页应用,你可以用它来与我们的模型对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have a studio offering that is an offering for our content creators that includes video, audio, image generation, and transcription.
zh: 我们还有一个面向内容创作者的 studio 产品,包括视频、音频、图像生成和转录。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why does privacy matter?
zh: 那么为什么隐私很重要?

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's deep dive into this.
zh: 让我们深入探讨一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as we know, data breaches are increasingly becoming an eventuality, which means that essentially reputational risk matters.
zh: 如我们所知,数据泄露正日益成为一种必然事件,这意味着声誉风险实际上很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You only need one data breach before your users stop trusting you and then move on to another provider.
zh: 你只需要一次数据泄露,用户就会不再信任你,然后转向另一个提供商。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if you're an enterprise, maybe you lose the enterprise customer who's been fueling almost 90% of your annual revenue.
zh: 或者如果你是一家企业,也许你会失去那个贡献了你几乎 90% 年收入的企业客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in this case, sensitive data can severely increase the impact of any security incident, as well as that, storing less user data directly reduces the blast radius of a security incident that happens.
zh: 所以在这种情况下,敏感数据会严重增加任何安全事件的影响,除此之外,存储更少的用户数据可以直接缩小发生的安全事件的波及范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how does Venice do privacy today?
zh: 那么 Venice 今天是如何做到隐私保护的呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, there's a few ways.
zh: 有几种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first way is that we don't store any prompts or conversations, of course, as we mentioned previously, which means that any digital footprint incurred in your site is essentially reduced to zero.
zh: 第一种方式是我们不存储任何提示词或对话,当然,正如我们之前提到的,这意味着你在我们网站上留下的数字足迹基本上降为零。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you use models like GLM 5.2 and Kimi 2.7, you can guarantee that none of your conversations will be saved on our site.
zh: 所以当你使用像 GLM 5.2 和 Kimi 2.7 这样的模型时,你可以保证你的任何对话都不会被保存在我们的网站上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be all stored locally.
zh: 所有内容都将在本地存储。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have predefined tiers of privacy.
zh: 我们还有预定义的隐私层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: So private by default means that the aforementioned measures apply.
zh: 默认私密意味着前述措施全部适用。

speaker: Unknown
en: For providers like OpenAI and Claude, we anonymize your user footprint so that they can't identify you from your
zh: 对于像 OpenAI 和 Claude 这样的提供商,我们会对你的用户足迹进行匿名化,使他们无法从你的

speaker: Unknown
en: Simply from your prompt or your request.
zh: 仅仅从你的提示词或请求中识别出你。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have models hosted in trusted execution environments, meaning that you can verifiably prove that your inference was run in a totally private process.
zh: 我们还有托管在可信执行环境中的模型,这意味着你可以可验证地证明你的推理是在一个完全私密的过程中运行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: As well as that, we also use a privacy-first software architecture.
zh: 除此之外,我们还使用隐私优先的软件架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for endpoints like video generation where you have to pull the endpoints, we store the results in a totally encrypted payload using split key custody, meaning that attackers can't access your data and neither can the team should their accounts be compromised.
zh: 对于像视频生成这样需要轮询端点的场景,我们使用分割密钥托管将结果存储在完全加密的载荷中,这意味着攻击者无法访问你的数据,即使团队自己的账户被入侵也一样无法访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just want to introduce you to the idea that not all systems are made equal.
zh: 所以我只是想向大家介绍这样一个理念:并非所有系统都是平等的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So not all systems are made private.
zh: 并非所有系统都是私密的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some companies may claim their systems are private, but they're not really.
zh: 有些公司可能声称他们的系统是私密的,但实际上并不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys know how it goes.
zh: 你们知道这是怎么回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So while models are a very important part of an agentic system, in fact, they're a vital part of the system, they are still only one part.
zh: 虽然模型是智能体系统中非常重要的一部分,事实上,它们是系统的关键部分,但它们仍然只是其中一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, to create a complete system to accompany an LLM in doing a task, you have to build an entire process around it.
zh: 而且事实上,要创建一个完整的系统来配合 LLM 完成任务,你必须围绕它构建一整套流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, these systems are also much more prone to data leakage and breaches.
zh: 然而,这些系统也更容易发生数据泄露和入侵。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the real question is, how can we optimize for this kind of problem?
zh: 所以真正的问题是,我们如何针对这类问题进行优化?

speaker: Unknown
en: So one example I just wanted to bring up was observability logging.
zh: 我想提出的一个例子是可观测性日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: So observability, as many of you know, is a core part of any serious production system today.
zh: 可观测性,正如你们许多人所知,是当今任何严肃的生产系统的核心组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just to break it down quickly, observability can be broken down into metrics, logs, and traces.
zh: 快速拆解一下,可观测性可以分为指标、日志和追踪。

speaker: Unknown
en: So traces are simply a span of work done over a unit of time.
zh: 追踪只是一个单位时间内完成的一段工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Metrics are simply numbers like counters, gauges, for instance.
zh: 指标就是数字,比如计数器、仪表等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And logs are the actual messages.
zh: 而日志就是实际的消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: So logging, as you all know, is actually pretty great for debugging, especially in production or dev environments.
zh: 日志,众所周知,其实对调试非常有用,尤其是在生产或开发环境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can also accidentally store prompts and secrets by default if you're not careful, which can also hold personal information.
zh: 但如果不小心,你也可能默认意外存储提示词和机密信息,这些信息也可能包含个人数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, when you use Venice, you don't need to worry about any of that.
zh: 然而,当你使用 Venice 时,你不需要担心任何这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's talk about how secrets can flow through a regular agent.
zh: 那么让我们来谈谈机密信息是如何流经一个普通智能体的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, let's say you're using OpenClaw.
zh: 举个例子,假设你在使用 OpenClaw。

speaker: Unknown
en: You send a user request that gets sent to an agent runtime.
zh: 你发送一个用户请求,该请求会被发送到智能体运行时。

speaker: Unknown
en: The runtime might need a secret that it will fetch from a 1Password Vault, for instance, or HashCorp Vault.
zh: 运行时可能需要一个密钥,比如它会从 1Password Vault 或 HashCorp Vault 中获取。

speaker: Unknown
en: The secret will then get sent to the LLM reasoning layer.
zh: 然后这个密钥会被发送到 LLM 推理层。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my god.
zh: 哦天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the reasoning layer will then make an API request through a tool call, which will then return the answer back to the user.
zh: 然后推理层会通过工具调用发起一个 API 请求,再把答案返回给用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, due to this, the way that it's architected, the secrets get fed directly to the LLM, which means it then may get used in training data.
zh: 然而,由于这种架构方式,密钥被直接喂给了 LLM,这意味着它之后可能会被用于训练数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of privacy-preserving patterns that work, one thing that we've used at Venice is storing hashes that represent IDs that we need as opposed to direct data.
zh: 说到可行的隐私保护模式,我们在 Venice 用过的一种方法是存储代表所需 ID 的哈希,而不是直接存储数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, if you need to identify a user for rate-limiting purposes,
zh: 比如说,如果你需要为了限流的目的识别一个用户,

speaker: Unknown
en: You might not want to use their direct user footprint directly.
zh: 你可能不想直接使用他们直接的用户足迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might want to store it as a hash, for instance, just so you can identify them without directly using any of their personal data.
zh: 你可能想把它存储为哈希,这样你就可以识别他们,而不直接使用他们的任何个人数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: As well as that, we encrypt data and store it in an inaccessible enclave used in split key custody.
zh: 除此之外,我们会对数据加密,并将其存储在用于分裂密钥保管的不可访问飞地中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for context, encryption keys are stored in two halves, a read half and a write half.
zh: 作为背景,加密密钥被存储为两半,一个读半钥和一个写半钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: By splitting these, the attacker cannot access the data due to needing both halves for the decryption to complete.
zh: 通过拆分这些密钥,攻击者无法访问数据,因为解密完成需要两半密钥。

speaker: Unknown
en: Additionally, you can use design patterns like handles that can be easily revoked.
zh: 此外,你可以使用像句柄这样易于撤销的设计模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a handle is simply an object that grants you access to something.
zh: 句柄就是一个授予你访问某种东西权限的对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, let's say you have a database pool using a handle.
zh: 比如说,假设你有一个使用句柄的数据库连接池。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you have the handle, you can access the database pool.
zh: 当你拥有句柄时,你就可以访问数据库连接池。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you don't,
zh: 当你没有句柄时,

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you can't access it.
zh: 你就无法访问它。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is very important, especially when you're using authorization like JSON web tokens or session keys.
zh: 这一点非常重要,尤其是当你使用像 JSON web token 或会话密钥这样的授权时。

speaker: Unknown
en: That may be a core part of your authorization system.
zh: 那可能是你授权系统的核心部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: As well as that, of course, engineering your prompts with privacy in mind can be very helpful for engineering teams who are using coding harnesses like Cursor and Claude Code.
zh: 除此之外,当然,带着隐私意识来设计你的提示词,对使用像 Cursor 和 Claude Code 这类编码工具的工程团队来说会非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of protecting agent-handled data, so essentially ensuring narrow agent scope to decrease risk.
zh: 至于保护智能体处理的数据,本质上是确保智能体范围收窄以降低风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, let's say you pull tools from an NCP server that may have 15, 20 different tools.
zh: 比如说,假设你从一个 NCP 服务器拉取工具,那个服务器可能有 15、20 个不同的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't really want to use all of them.
zh: 你其实并不想使用所有这些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: You actually only really need one.
zh: 你实际上通常只需要其中一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you also need an API key to handle that API call.
zh: 但你还需要一个 API 密钥来处理那个 API 调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you pull that API key in from your password vault and then you send it as part of the agent, what can happen is that it gets exfiltrated through the agent on a tool call to whatever web server is being hosted by a bad actor, for instance.
zh: 所以如果你从密码库中取出那个 API 密钥,然后把它作为智能体的一部分发送出去,可能发生的情况是,它会在工具调用中通过智能体被泄露给某个由恶意行为者托管的网络服务器,比如说。

speaker: Unknown
en: As well as that,
zh: 除此之外,

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have a classification layer in front of an agent to check for prompt injection, for example.
zh: 我们还会在智能体前面加一个分类层,用来检查提示词注入之类的威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a couple of ways you can do this.
zh: 有几种方法可以做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can either use an LLM-based layer to do this, or you can alternatively use a semantic search layer, for example, using Vector Search via something like Quadrant, LanceDB, or additionally, you can use an in-memory process
zh: 你可以使用基于 LLM 的层来做这件事,或者你也可以使用语义搜索层,比如通过 Quadrant、LanceDB 之类的向量搜索,另外,你还可以使用内存中的进程

speaker: Unknown
en: It should also be noted that tight context loops caused by narrow agent scope can also improve context window performance.
zh: 还应该指出,由收窄智能体范围带来的紧凑上下文循环,也可以改善上下文窗口的性能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, because you don't have as many tools, your agents may be able to perform much better.
zh: 比如说,因为你的工具没有那么多,你的智能体可能能够表现得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's well known that when you fill your context window, by doing so, when you reach near the limits of your context window, performance can actually degrade considerably.
zh: 众所周知,当你填满上下文窗口时,当你接近上下文窗口的极限时,性能实际上可能会显著下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: By keeping an empty or near empty context window, we can make sure that the agent is performing at its best.
zh: 通过保持一个空的或接近空的上下文窗口,我们可以确保智能体发挥出最佳水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's look at keeping secrets out of the model.
zh: 那么我们来看看如何让密钥远离模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here we have a user request that gets sent to the reasoning layer.
zh: 这里我们有一个用户请求,它被发送到推理层。

speaker: Unknown
en: This reasoning layer is actually then formulating a series of non-deterministic inputs for an agentic runtime.
zh: 这个推理层实际上是在为一个智能体运行时生成一系列非确定性输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by tying the password vaults to the agentic runtime instead of the reasoning layer, what happens then is that the agent runtime is essentially turned into an execution layer, which then we can consider it deterministic.
zh: 通过把密码库绑定到智能体运行时而不是推理层,接下来发生的事情就是,智能体运行时本质上变成了一个执行层,我们可以认为它是确定性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can do all kinds of things that you normally wouldn't be able to do for privacy and security reasons at the LLM layer.
zh: 我们可以做一些在 LLM 层出于隐私和安全原因通常做不到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, let's say you want to use a browser user tool and you need to log into a website that requires your credentials.
zh: 比如说,假设你想使用一个浏览器用户工具,并且需要登录一个需要你的凭据的网站。

speaker: Unknown
en: With this software architecture, it's much more reasonable to say that it's private and secure rather than feeding your password directly into the reasoning layer.
zh: 有了这种软件架构,说它是私密且安全的就合理得多,而不是把你的密码直接喂进推理层。

speaker: Unknown
en: As well as, you know, calling external APIs.
zh: 同样适用于,你知道的,调用外部 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of sandboxing your agents, it's a very well-known fact that using sandboxes and VMs, for example, Firecracker and you know, AWS EC2 in a VPC can significantly upgrade the security of your agent.
zh: 至于给你的智能体做沙箱隔离,这是一个众所周知的事实:使用沙箱和虚拟机,比如 Firecracker,以及你知道的,在 VPC 中使用 AWS EC2,可以显著提升你智能体的安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, this doesn't act as a cure-all for your agentic systems.
zh: 然而,这并不是你的智能体系统的万能药。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, if you have internet access enabled for your agent, it can still accidentally exfiltrate data through external API access if you're not careful.
zh: 比如说,如果你的智能体启用了互联网访问,如果你不小心,它仍然可能通过外部 API 访问意外泄露数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore, monitoring permissions is essential.
zh: 因此,监控权限是必不可少的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my personal suggestion is
zh: 所以我个人的建议是

speaker: Unknown
en: Building your own agentic runtime.
zh: 构建你自己的智能体运行时。

speaker: Unknown
en: So essentially building your own coding harnesses where you can add your own steps, your own observability, your own tools, things of that nature.
zh: 所以本质上就是在构建你自己的编码 harness,你可以在其中加入自己的步骤、自己的可观测性、自己的工具,诸如此类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially owning the execution layer and reasoning layer.
zh: 本质上就是把执行层和推理层掌握在自己手里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's talk about privacy at the hardware level very quickly.
zh: 那我们快速聊一下硬件层面的隐私。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of this, there's something I like to call confidential compute, where a trusted execution environment essentially at the hardware level enables the inference process to be run privately.
zh: 在这方面,有一种我喜欢称之为机密计算的东西,即可信执行环境本质上在硬件层面让推理过程能够私密地运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with Venice, how this works is that when you send a request, you get a response.
zh: 以 Venice 为例,它的工作方式是:当你发送一个请求,你会得到一个响应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we actually return an attestation that you can then
zh: 然后我们实际上会返回一个认证证明(attestation),你可以随后

speaker: Unknown
en: Verify with our Attestation Verifier.
zh: 用我们的 Attestation Verifier 来验证它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of this, what this actually means is that you can fully isolate an agent at the reasoning layer cryptographically and prove it.
zh: 就此而言,这实际上意味着你可以在密码学层面完全隔离推理层上的一个智能体,并且能证明这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of confidential tool calls, there is still some work to be done.
zh: 至于机密工具调用,还有一些工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: TEs are still great for tool calls.
zh: 可信执行环境(TE)对工具调用来说仍然很好用。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, we also offer end-to-end encryption, but there's also some work to be done there because of the need to provide an ergonomic API experience.
zh: 不过,我们也提供端到端加密,但这方面也还有一些工作要做,因为需要提供一个符合人体工学的 API 体验,

speaker: Unknown
en: while still allowing users to return entirely encrypted tool calls.
zh: 同时仍然允许用户返回完全加密的工具调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is still kind of an ongoing challenge.
zh: 这仍然算是一个持续的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of this, a very reliable solution would be to allow providers to own the compute layer at which your tool call is being run.
zh: 就此而言,一个非常可靠的解决方案是让提供商掌控你的工具调用运行所在的计算层。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, sorry, just give me a sec.
zh: 不过,抱歉,让我等一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of confidential tool calls, yeah, there's definitely some work to be done.
zh: 所以关于机密工具调用,是的,确实还有一些工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's it.
zh: 是的,就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for listening.
zh: 感谢收听。
